To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proteasome is an essential component of the MHC class I pathway, and that its subunit composition is critical for the generation of MCH class I ligands, and thus, for the immune responses of CD8 T cells.
the proteasome is a central player in the generation of antigenic peptides and the regulation of immune responses.
the proteasome subunits PA28, LMP2, LMP7 and MECL-1 are important for CD8 T cell activation and survival and that thymoproteosomes are involved in the selection of the TCR repertoire in the thymus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of proteasomes during antigen processing and immune responses.
understanding how proteasome composition and function is regulated by cell-intrinsic and extrinsic signals and how this affects immune cell development and responses.
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which the UPS contributes to the generation of MCH class I ligands in the thymus and the periphery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UPS is a highly versatile system, which can be adapted to a variety of different functions depending on cell type, developmental stage or stimuli received.
the UPS is an essential component of the immune response.
proteasomes are involved in all aspects of immune responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteasome is a central player in the generation of peptide ligands for MHC class I molecules, which are presented on the cell surface and trigger CD8 T cell immunity.
the UPS plays a central role in the regulation of the immune system and that its dysregulation contributes to autoimmune diseases and cancer.
the proteasome is a central player in the regulation of immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the different proteasome subtypes are not merely a reflection of the different cellular environments but rather contribute in a specific manner to the generation of immunogenic peptides and immune responses.
the UPS is a versatile and highly regulated proteolytic machinery that plays a key role in immune cell development and function.

the proteasome plays an important role in immune responses by regulating MHC class I presentation of antigenic peptides, T cell repertoire development, and the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
